sekcje: Drug Levels and Effects > Summary of Use during Lactation

Lemongrass (Cymbopogon citratus) essential oil contains alpha-terpineole, alpha-pinene, beta-myrcene, geraniol, limonene, and verbenene. Lemongrass has been included in some mixtures promoted to increase milk supply; however, no scientifically valid clinical trials support this use. Galactogogues should never replace evaluation and counseling on modifiable factors that affect milk production. Lemongrass essential oil extract is “generally recognized as safe” (GRAS) in foods by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration. Rare cases of liver toxicity and allergic sensitization have occurred with lemongrass. Two aroma therapists became allergic to their essential oils as demonstrated on patch testing, developing dermatitis on the hands and forearms. One of them subsequently developed a small area of dermatitis on her forearm following ingestion of lemongrass tea and Thai food. Elevated liver enzymes occurred in a woman taking Mother’s Milk Tea, which contains West Indian lemongrass leaf.
